title: Soft-commitment risk annotator — Emilia Cortez
content:
Quick brain dump and working rubric — trying to capture soft commitments and how they map to measurable ramp risks. Notes to self, rough and fragmented.

Context: took loop with candidate (backend/runtime-systems focus). Candidate: Priya Sen (pseudonym used internally), loop date 2025-10-30. This file is my private scratch for hiring sync.

High-level impression (first-pass):
- Technically very competent on CUDA-level reasoning and KV cache behavior, but tends to hedge on operational tradeoffs (prefers ideal designs over pragmatic constraints).
- Communicates clearly when discussing latency tradeoffs; less clear about prioritization under time pressure.
- Expressed a strong preference for building new primitives rather than using existing infra — signal: builder > operator.

Soft-commitment signals observed (what candidate said vs likely follow-through):
- "I would prefer to rewrite the batcher to remove tail latency spikes" — high enthusiasm for rewrites; risk = tendency to over-index on perfect design. (Annotate: likely to push larger PRs vs incremental ops work.)
- "I want ownership of rollout strategy and can drive canaries" — explicit ownership ask; positive for ownership but unknown execution bias. (Risk: may expect product support or special cases.)
- "I like to pair and mentor; I prefer weekly deep-collabs" — cultural fit for mentoring; positive signal for team ramp.

Mapping to ramp risks (concrete):
- Short-term (0–3 months):
  - Risk A: Blocks triage responsiveness during on-call due to focus on deep design work. Mitigation: schedule explicit on-call pairing shadowing and small ownership tasks.
  - Risk B: Latency fixes vs product deadlines conflict. Mitigation: define short win list with measurable SLO gains.
- Medium-term (3–9 months):
  - Risk C: Rewrites consuming sprint cycles. Mitigation: require technical design PRD + stakeholder signoff for >2-week initiatives.
  - Risk D: Tooling/infra ownership gaps if candidate drives bespoke solutions. Mitigation: pair candidate with infra PM and ensure contribution to shared libraries.

Concrete signals to validate in hiring loop (things we can ask / probe next):
- Ask for a recent example where they deliberately chose an incremental fix over a rewrite; reason and outcome.
- Present a hypothetical: rollout must prioritize throughput improvements for a top-tier customer while preserving product deadlines for new features — ask for concrete tradeoffs and a rollout plan (timeline, metrics, fallback).
- Request a 30-min whiteboard on a lightweight batching change (limited scope) to see tradeoff granularity and speed of decision.

Behavioral notes / quotes (verbatim where possible):
- "If the batcher is wrong at the kernel boundary, we end up debugging for weeks." — strong mental model for low-level failure modes.
- "I'd rather not own messy legacy; I'd rather build the component right." — red flag for operator willingness.

Scorecard (subjective quick numbers, 1–5):
- System design (LLM infra focus): 4
- Low-level performance intuition (kernels/TVM/CUDA): 5
- Production ops/incident response: 3
- Cross-team pragmatism / tradeoffs: 3
- Mentorship / team culture: 4
- Overall hire recommendation: lean-hire with caveats (see mitigations)

Suggested hiring outcome and next steps:
- Recommendation: advance to final sync with SRE partner + PM to explicitly probe incident behavior and product tradeoffs. If proceeding to offer, make ramp expectations explicit in offer: 3-month milestones (on-call pairing completed, one infra PR merged to shared libs, measurable latency contribution).
- If borderline: keep on bench for a later infra-focused IC role with heavier design remit (more appropriate than immediate on-call heavy SRE tilt).

Open questions / unresolved: (keepers for follow-ups)
- How comfortable will candidate be handling immediate P1s during first 60 days? (Need a live scenario in next loop)
- Will candidate collaborate on incremental refactors or push for end-to-end redesigns? (Ask for a concrete decision-making example)
- Compensation expectations relative to level — they signaled preference for more ownership rather than title; ensure alignment before final offer.

Operational checklist (for hiring manager if moving forward):
- [ ] Book 30-min with SRE lead to run a real incident post-mortem roleplay.
- [ ] Ask candidate for 1–2 past PR links showing small-to-medium scope changes (prefer ops-focused).
- [ ] Draft 3-month ramp milestones into offer letter.
- [ ] Pair candidate with Marcus Lee for batcher design micro-critique.

Scratchy closing thoughts:
- Candidate brings rare kernel-level intuition which is high value for runtime. Biggest risk is mismatch on operator vs builder expectations — can probably be mitigated with upfront ramping structure.
- My gut: hire if we can make the role explicit about gradual ownership and concrete ops deliverables.

Notes to self: convert these into a short blurb for the panel (1–2 sentences) and add to the interview artifacts. Keep this doc private; intentionally informal.

-- Emilia
